patch.value: The release workflow pins a pm CLI three weeks older than CI's, and its changelog reads are bounded

This repository pins two different pm CLI versions. CI installs 2026.8.21 to run pm health with merge drivers required; the release workflow installs 2026.8.6 for all three of its pm-changelog invocations. That older pin is not neutral: its pm health invocation is known to hang, so any step that reaches for health inside the release job inherits a silent stall rather than a failure, and the two pins disagree about item hashing, which is what makes a history drift verdict depend on which binary produced it. Separately, none of the three invocations passes the unbounded output budget and output limit controls every other fleet package passes. pm-github proved that fuse is real: it kept releasing until its tracker reached eighty-six items, then failed for ten consecutive days on a read truncated to five.
Both workflows install the same exact pm CLI version; every pm-changelog invocation in the release workflow requests a complete unbounded workspace read

value.author: claude
value.text: Both workflows now install @unbrained/pm-cli 2026.8.21, and the release workflow's pm-changelog moves from 2026.8.6 to 2026.8.22 to match the rest of the fleet. All three invocations request a complete unbounded workspace read. The forwarding is proven rather than assumed: running the pinned generator with --pm-arg naming a flag pm does not have returns pm's own unknown_option error for that flag, so the arguments reach the binary and the controls are not inert.
